P1.evidence: P1a clean: "Look, I went through some of the notes that you spoke with Kim about, yeah? And so I have some idea on where you're at right now", then read back specifics (age 50, UK, 16 kg kettlebell, adjustable dumbbells, diabetes as priority). P1b missed — no four-part frame; he framed only purpose and fit: "I'm kind of old school, and I would like to hear it also from you, so to fill in any gaps, and that will help me to actually assess if this is the good thing for you." P1c partial — he got a soft "Exactly" rather than an explicit "Does that work?" agreement. P1d missed — he never asked what the prospect was looking for help with; he asserted the priority from the setter notes instead: "your number one priority from what Kim said is getting your diabetes in check."

P2.evidence: Strong factual baseline. P2a partial — age confirmed from setter notes ("I know, like, you're 50, right?"), but height was never asked and the 88 kg bodyweight was volunteered unprompted at 00:38:42, which the spec scores as not-asked. P2b hit: "And your job is mostly sedentary, or how does it look like?" P2c hit — diabetes explored at length, though hereditary conditions were never asked about. P2d hit: "So about injuries and any constraints that you might have on your body" and follow-ups on the knee and back. P2e hit: "walk me through, like, what your training looks like right now on a typical week" plus "And how many times per week?" and the honesty push "So was it three times or less?" P2f partial — the HbA1c results history came volunteered. P2g hit: "let's get to the very important thing in terms of diabetes, which is nutrition. How does it look like for you right now? And please be brutally honest." P2h partial — sleep was probed only as a behaviour cause ("Why are you not going to bed early?"), never for quantity or quality. P2i miss — energy through the day never asked.

P3.evidence: The best phase of the call. P3d hit twice: "for you, when you think about getting diabetes genuinely under control, what does that actually mean for you? Like what changes?" and the excellent "What's behind that phrase, physical potential?" He then went one layer further than the script with "And when you actually say it out loud right now, how does that sit with you?", which produced "Not good, man. It makes you a bit emotional, to honest." P3g hit — he drove it to family: "It's another layer here, not only diabetes, which is your health, but being there for your family, because diabetes is a serious condition." P3h hit — "correct me if I'm wrong, if I'm totally off, this is about your health and longevity", answered "Absolutely." P3a and P3c never asked; the six-pack framing came from the prospect unprompted. P3f partial — the kids were volunteered first ("I have two teenage kids. I need to be and I want to be better for them"); the rep only followed up on them.

P4.evidence: P4a/P4b hit: "Share some light on the diets that you've been following" drew out carnivore, keto and the bodybuilder who got his HbA1c to under 6. P4c/P4d hit: "and this lack of consistency, where does it come from?" and later "what was the reason for, of not being consistent in terms of nutrition?" P4e hit — the prospect named the gap himself: "I need consistency. The reason why there is a lack of consistency is because I have always easily gone to food at any time", and named the root behind that as childhood trauma. P4f partial — the rep stated the conclusion rather than asking it: "you know this works. You already felt it... the issue has never been that around the method itself. It's about the consistency." Correct content, but delivered as a statement, so the prospect never had to answer why he cannot stick to it alone.

P5.evidence: P5a run well and almost verbatim: "if nothing actually changes, and we are sitting here in two years or five years, and everything is more or less the same, or probably worse... what does that look like for you? Like, not medically, but in terms of your actual life?" The prospect gave a strong answer — "You and I both already know the answer. And it's not good." The rep then abandoned the frame. He never asked whether that was something the prospect was willing to settle for, never asked why not, and never asked for a line in the sand. He instead took a light accountability detour ("who's responsible for making that change?") and moved straight into presenting the programme. The emotional charge generated at 00:31 was left unconverted, and it is the direct reason the later commitment check had nothing to lean on.

P6.evidence: Sequencing is inverted. The script requires a genuine verbal yes BEFORE presenting anything; the rep presented all three pillars first and only then asked "let me ask you this, like, are you committed to doing the work?" at 00:52:20. P6a partial — mid-presentation he asked "do you believe if you had all that dialed in that would move the needle for you", which is a belief question about the mechanism, not about the prospect getting there with the right structure and the right person; the answer was also deflected to the general case: "I think it would move the needle for anybody." P6b never asked — the "if you had everything you needed, is there any reason you wouldn't go all in" question is exactly what would have surfaced the competing diabetes specialist while there was still call left to work with. P6c miss — hesitation surfaced immediately and the rep did not return to Phase 5, he accepted the hold and closed the call.

P11.evidence: No close was attempted and no price was ever named, so the payment and onboarding phase was never reachable. Worth noting for coaching rather than scoring: the rep had explicit permission to present — "Okay, Shahz, you poured in my heart a lot of confidence. And I would like to invite you to work with Trevor, because there is life on the line" — and still never made an offer.

objection_plays.detail: Trigger landed in substance at 00:53:25 — "why don't we put this conversation on hold?" No moves ran. He did not ask whether the prospect felt what they had gone through could get him to his goal, did not ask what was actually preventing him from getting started, did not use "thinking isn't the problem, deciding is", and did not run the identity close. He answered with "Right. I respect that and I appreciate you being upfront and honest. Let's do that." Given the emotional material already on the table — waste, the kids, the grandfather, "I want my life back" — this was the cheapest available play and none of it was used.

Competing specialist provider: "I'm due to potentially have a conversation next week with another trainer because he, unlike other trainers, is a specialist in diabetes." There is no scripted play for a prospect who is shopping a clinically specialised competitor, and this is a real gap — it sits alongside the two already logged in known_gaps_in_script. The prospect's presenting problem is a diagnosed metabolic disease, and the programme was sold on generic kettlebell mechanics with no clinical positioning at all. Even without a script the rep had obvious room: ask what the specialist would provide, ask what he would need to see, or book the reconvene call there and then. He did none of these and left the follow-up as an open-ended prospect-initiated email.
No money objection was possible — no price was ever presented and finances were never discussed.
A wife is referenced as motivation ("I think my wife deserves better from me") but never as a decision-maker or a consult requirement.
No timing objection. The prospect's delay is competitor evaluation, not readiness — he was explicit that timings were not an issue: "In terms of the timings, I don't mind that. I'm all for that."
No fear or doubt about the modality. He is pre-sold on kettlebells: "I think kettlebells is a really good way forward for me, even if it's not with you."

notes: Textbook first half, no second half. Discovery, root cause and the emotional bridge were genuinely excellent and got a guarded man to say "I feel a lot of waste has happened" — then the rep never converted any of it, skipped the settle/line-in-sand close of Phase 5, presented before getting commitment, named no price and folded on the first objection. The single actionable coaching point: run P5b-d and P6b before presenting, so the competing diabetes specialist surfaces at minute 30 with the consequence frame still live, not at minute 52 with nothing left to work with. Second point: he had explicit invitation-level permission and still made no offer.
